newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba property unit chief bailed-prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: Veba property unit chief bailed-prosecutors.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Wednesday that Ulrich Lilienthal, chairman of the property unit of utility Veba AG, had been set free on bail.
He had been in investigative custody on suspicion of fraud since June 27.
Prosecutors suspect Lilienthal, his predecessor Ludwig Staender and a further nine employees of the company of using company funds to pay for private construction contracts.
A spokesman for state legal authorities in Bochum said that the investigations were continuing.

Lilienthal was suspended from his position as chairman of Veba Immobilien on June 30. The spokesman said he was bailed for a six-figure sum and prosecutors said there was no danger of the suspect absconding.
Staender, who was first detained last Friday, will remain in custody.
Veba said it would request an economic auditing group to examine the charges and thereafter make the necessary decisions on the matter.
